newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia bank sells HRK171 mln bills, rates mixed.
newsitem.headline: Croatia bank sells HRK171 mln bills, rates mixed.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sold 170.8 million kuna in five- and 13-week bills at mixed rates at a weekly auction on Wednesday.
Volume rose from only 57 million kuna last week as commercial banks' liquidity improved and rates rose marginally.
Five-week bills were issued on volume of 141 million kuna at 8.0 percent, unchanged from last Wednesday. But the 13-week rate edged up to 9.50 from 9.39 percent two weeks ago.
For full results see page NBHT.
An official said the central bank drained 3.05 billion kuna from the banking system through Monday's reserve payment.
It would repay banks 99.2 million today that was tied up in mandatory bills as an additional reserve requirement.

The National Bank of Croatia has cut October's reserve ratio 1.1 points to 35.85 percent of kuna deposits. But analysts said total obligation could still go up because of an expected rise in total deposits. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
